chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Bechet's Blue Note Jazzmen and Columbia sides
summary: Welburn lists more Bechet sessions; Moore remembers Tiger Rag, Tin Roof Blues and Sister Kate.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Then, just while we're on Bechet, and you've done some work with Bechet... There's a quartet with Pops Foster and Lloyd Philips on Columbia, where you play "Buddy Bolden's Stomp" and "My Woman Blues." That was put out by Columbia. And then there's Bechet's Blue Note Jazzmen. That's Art Hodes, Walter Page is on bass, and Wild Bill Davidson. There's "Sister Kate," or I guess the full title is "I wish I Could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate" (these were for Blue Note), "Tiger Rag," "Tin Roof Blues," "I've Found A New Baby," "Nobody Knows You When You're Down And Out" and "When the Saints Go Marching In." So that was yet another Blue Note recording that you made with Sidney Bechet. And of course, Hodes was a member of the section at that time.
Do you remember any of these recording sessions?

Well, during that time I remember... I remember doing "Tiger Rag." I probably do remember those sessions. "Tiger Rag," "Save It, Pretty Mama," "Way Down Yonder In New Orleans," yeah... What is the name of that other one you called there?
Yeah. I was on that session. "Sister Kate."
